findings.F1: Across the 930 short blocks the mean excess fall is only 0.07% per 10 bars (t 0.16, hit rate 52.5%), against a block-to-block spread of 14.0%, so any edge is buried in the market's own 10-day moves.
findings.F2: The sign of the result flips by year: shorts gained in 2018 (+3.9%, t 2.32, n 134) and 2022 (+2.3%, t 2.48, n 195), but lost in 2020 (−4.3%, t −2.73, n 88) and 2021 (−5.1%, t −2.32, n 74), and these cancel in the pooled mean.
findings.F3: The windows split the same way, from w9 (+4.0%, t 3.71) and w7 (+5.8%, t 3.35) to w23 (−6.7%, t −3.12) and w21 (−3.6%, t −2.75), while no coin stands out (coin means range from −0.39% to +0.56%, all |t| < 0.6).
findings.F4: Sitting deeper below the average does not help: the deepest forecast bucket (−20 to −10) gives −0.15% (t −0.17, n 294), the −10 to −5 bucket gives +0.64% (t 0.76), and the slope of excess return on allocation has the wrong sign (−0.0056).
findings.F5: Shorts gained most when the 200-day average itself had fallen more than 5% over the prior 20 bars: +1.6% excess fall (t 1.74, hit 54.8%, n 217), against roughly 0% where the average was flat or rising (−0.58% to +0.44%, all |t| < 0.7).
findings.F6: Timing since the cross matters but is not steady: the first 10 bars below the average give +1.7% (t 1.34, n 155), bars 10–30 give −1.95% (t −1.94, n 224), and bars 60–120 give +1.7% (t 1.81, n 210).
findings.F7: The share of coins below their own averages adds little on its own: with a falling average and broad weakness the shorts gain +0.66% (t 0.95, n 353), and this pocket still swings by year, +4.8% (t 2.95) in 2018 against −2.9% in 2020.

ideas.idea: When a coin's close is below its 200-day average and that average has itself been falling steeply over the past few weeks, the coin keeps falling over the next 10 days by more than its usual drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader would take shorts below the long average only when the average is already turning down hard, and refuse them when the average is flat or rising.
ideas.name: steeply falling long average

ideas.idea: In the first days after a coin's close crosses below its 200-day average, the coin keeps falling over the next 10 days by more than its usual drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader would short only fresh crosses below the long average rather than holding a short for the whole time the price stays below it.
ideas.name: fresh cross below continues
